Would discovering civilization ruins on Venus change your stance on anthropomorphic climate change?

No because Venus' atmosphere is not simply an out-of-whack version of Earth's atmosphere and does not lend towards a direct comparison. Venus' atmosphere is 90+ times higher in mass/pressure and is composed of about 96% CO2. That goes far beyond what the idea of anthropogenic climate change would do before life would be driven to extinction. While many climatologists like to point to Venus as a good example of what human caused climate change can lead to, I think it is highly disingenuous to make the comparison because Venus is what it is today by processes that didn't involve life. If anything that makes Venus a better example for extreme climate change being caused by natural processes. Discovering ancient ruins of civilization on Venus would make me think that Venutian life was destroyed by natural climate processes instead of sentient interference.

For the record, I do not deny climate change. I do however remain skeptical that there are only two choices in the matter: caused by man or natural. Climate as a system is extremely complex and I don't think we understand it enough to make models and predictions that are remotely accurate enough to point the finger at any cause. Science does not work on faith or consensus.
